subject: PO vs Card: Procurement follow-up & next steps
messages:
From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@finopsco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Torres <michael@finopsco.com>
Date: 2027-02-09T17:12:00Z
Subject: RE: PO vs Card - quick follow-up after demo

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo today — the team appreciated the walkthrough of Redwood's runtime and the cost/latency controls. A couple of procurement items I promised to follow up on after our call: 

- AP policy: For any vendor spend > $10k/year we need a PO and vendor onboarding (KYB + security questionnaire). Smaller purchases can sometimes go through on corporate card but need to be routed through our marketplace if the vendor is listed.
- Vendor onboarding: They require an onboarding packet + W9 and a standard vendor form; timelines for completion are typically 5–7 business days once we receive the packet and SOW.
- Marketplace: We're onboarding vendors to our internal marketplace which allows card payments and automatic tax handling; curious if Redwood is open to being listed or if you prefer direct invoicing.

Quick Qs:
1) For an initial pilot (3 months, estimated $8–12k), can we pay by card via a marketplace listing or does Redwood require a PO for pilots?
2) If we need a PO, do you have a standard SOW + vendor packet to expedite?

I'll loop in procurement next week if we have the paperwork ready. Appreciate any notes on typical timelines and who from your side owns vendor onboarding.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Li
Head of Procurement | FinOpsCo

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@finopsco.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-10T13:09:00Z
Subject: RE: PO vs Card - quick follow-up after demo

Hi Samantha — great to meet you (virtually) today. 

Summary and options based on what you shared: 

1) Pilot / Card option (recommended for fast time-to-value)\- If FinOpsCo can pay through your marketplace, we can accept card payments for the initial pilot (~$8–12k). That usually avoids the PO cycle and gets you up and running in days rather than weeks. We are open to being listed — we can provide the vendor profile and tax docs for marketplace onboarding.

2) PO / Direct invoice (recommended for committed/enterprise deployments)\- For spend > $10k/year or longer-term Dedicated capacity, we typically operate on a PO + net-30 invoice. We have a standard SOW and vendor onboarding packet we can share to accelerate procurement. Onboarding + PO issuance usually takes 5–10 business days depending on your AP queue.

Attachments I attached: Redwood_SOW_V1.pdf (template SOW), Vendor_Onboarding_Form.xlsx (vendor packet) — these should cover the onboarding questions you mentioned (we'll provide W9 and proof of insurance on request).

Next steps I propose: 
- If you want to move quickly, confirm marketplace/card path and I will send the vendor profile + DPA + W9.
- If you need the PO path, I can provide a redline-friendly SOW and coordinate with our legal team for any quick clarifications.
- Proposed procurement check-in: Tue 2027-02-15 10:00 AM PT — happy to join.

Let me know which route you'd prefer and I’ll prioritize the paperwork.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_SOW_V1.pdf; Vendor_Onboarding_Form.xlsx
